poetryFrame.leftVertical: THE HEIGHT IS BEAUTIFUL, BUT THE VIEW IS EMPTY OF YOUR VOICE
poetryFrame.rightVertical: I AM ONLY THE ONE WHO PUT YOU THERE TO SEE HOW HIGH YOU CAN RISE
poetryFrame.bottomLine: THIS DISTANCE SPEAKS VOLUMES I CANNOT READ
sonnetLines: The fall was cushioned by my steady hand,
A gentle lift from shadows deep below.
But heights are learned in shifting, barren sand,
Where seeds of fragile independence grow.
You climb so high to prove you do not need,
To grasp the anchor that has held you fast.
I planted faith like a necessary creed,
A future built on moments of the past.
The lonely name against the fading blue,
As dawn reveals the cost of every grace.
We build our lives with promises untrue,
And leave no comfort in this empty space.
So tell me now, when nothing holds you near,
What echoes whisper when I am not here?
